newsitem.title: KUWAIT: British government to maintain Iran trade-adviser.
newsitem.headline: British government to maintain Iran trade-adviser.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government is expected to maintain trade links with Iran despite difficulties in dealing with the Islamic republic, a British trade adviser said on Tuesday.

"There are still a lot of decisions to be made on how Iran will be approached," the Director of the Committee For Middle East Trade (COMET), Ron Hollis, said of his preliminary talks with the new British government.
But the "incoming government made it clear that the policy would be an open trade policy," he told reporters in Kuwait. "I think trade with Iran will continue with the scale we have at the moment."
He put Britain's exports to Iran at almost 400 million stg ($652 million) a year but did not have a figure for British imports from Iran.
COMET, a British government sponsored body, advises British industry and the government on export and investment opportunities in the Arab world, Iran and Turkey.
"There are problems on both sides but overall I believe trade will continue with Iran, said Hollis, adding that "Trade with Iraq is impossible, trade with Iran is difficult".
Iraq is under wide United Nations sanctions since its 1990 invasion of Kuwait while the United States has imposed unilateral sanctions on Iran.
With Kuwait the trade balance is in favour of Britain with exports, including military hardware, valued at 580 million pounds a year compared with 180 million pounds in Kuwaiti exports.
Hollis stressed that in general the value of invisible trade was often equal to that of visible trade, adding that the imbalance issue was discussed with Kuwaiti officials.
He said the gap could be narrowed if Kuwait pushed ahead with several proposed laws to attract foreign investment to the oil-rich tiny Gulf Arab state.
